name: Hanoi
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Hanoi: FDI partner and supplier diligence, state-linked counterparty research and VIAC arbitration support.
hero_lede: Hanoi is Vietnam's capital and the seat of its ministries, central bank and highest court, and a growing base for foreign manufacturing and technology investment. Investigative work connected to the city often concerns state-linked counterparties, licensing and land, and partners in northern Vietnam's industrial supply chains.
intro: Hanoi is Vietnam's political capital and the economic centre of the north. Reporting based on city statistics put Hanoi at about 12.6 percent of national GRDP and 8.1 percent of the national population in 2022, and its master plan projects around 12 million people by 2030. The city has attracted cumulative registered foreign investment of about US$61.5 billion across more than 7,700 projects, second nationally, with Japan, Singapore and South Korea the leading sources. Manufacturing and processing, engineering, electronics assembly, real estate, retail and services are major activities, alongside Hoa Lac Hi-Tech Park and industrial zones served by Noi Bai International Airport.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Hanoi because it is where licences, land allocations, major contracts and policy decisions are made, and where many state-owned groups and their affiliates are headquartered. Foreign investors entering joint ventures, acquiring local companies or appointing distributors need to understand who stands behind a Hanoi counterparty, its relationships with public bodies and its record in land and construction. Manufacturers moving supply chains into northern Vietnam need supplier checks. Anti-corruption campaigns have led to prosecutions of officials and business people in recent years, so reputational and integrity research before a transaction carries particular weight.

matters.title: Joint venture partner background research
matters.text: Researching Hanoi companies and their owners before a joint venture or acquisition, including enterprise registration history, changes of legal representative and charter capital, related companies, litigation, enforcement notices and press coverage, and any links to state-owned groups or officials that affect how the partner wins contracts.

matters.title: Land and real estate counterparties
matters.text: Reviewing Hanoi developers and landholders for investors and lenders, with attention to land use right allocations, project approvals, delays, buyer disputes and any connection to land-related prosecutions, which have featured in Vietnam's anti-corruption enforcement in recent years.

matters.title: Northern supply chain verification
matters.text: Verifying suppliers and subcontractors in Hanoi's industrial zones and surrounding provinces for manufacturers relocating production, checking that the entity exists as described, who owns it, whether it has related-party links to the buyer's staff, and whether it has disputes or compliance issues.

matters.title: Procurement and licensing integrity
matters.text: Assessing intermediaries, consultants and agents who help foreign companies with ministry approvals, licences or public tenders in Hanoi, looking at their ownership, government relationships, fee structures and any history in investigations, as part of an anti-bribery compliance review.

matters.title: Research for VIAC and court proceedings
matters.text: Supporting counsel in arbitrations administered by the Vietnam International Arbitration Centre and in Hanoi court proceedings with background on parties and witnesses and identification of corporate interests and assets, so that claims, settlement positions and enforcement steps rest on verified information.

local_context.title: Courts sitting in Hanoi
local_context.text: The Supreme People's Court sits in Hanoi, together with the Hanoi People's Court and regional people's courts under the court structure in place since 1 July 2025. The Hanoi People's Court has long carried a large commercial caseload; commentary has noted hundreds of economic disputes a year there. Hanoi courts also hear applications to set aside arbitral awards seated in the city, which makes their approach important for parties to Hanoi arbitrations.

local_context.title: Arbitration centres in Hanoi
local_context.text: The Vietnam International Arbitration Centre is the country's best known arbitral institution, and arbitration is governed by the Law on Commercial Arbitration 2010, under which disputes must arise from commercial activity or involve a party engaged in it. Courts have set aside VIAC awards where a dispute was held to be civil rather than commercial. Other centres are expanding: the Southern Trade Arbitration Center opened a Hanoi branch in 2026.

local_context.title: Enterprise registration and filings
local_context.text: Companies in Hanoi register with the city's business registration office and appear on the National Business Registration Portal, which shows basic data such as registration number, address, legal representative and changes published in notices. Foreign-invested projects also hold investment registration certificates. Shareholder detail, financial statements and court documents generally need to be obtained through counsel or the company, and availability varies by record type.

local_context.title: Regulators and state bodies
local_context.text: National regulators are headquartered in Hanoi, including the State Bank of Vietnam and the State Securities Commission, as are the ministries that issue many investment and sector licences. The Hanoi Stock Exchange operates in the city, and many state-owned groups have their head offices there. Regulatory decisions, sanctions published by securities and tax authorities, and listed-company disclosures are valuable sources for counterparty research.

local_context.title: City statistics and investment bodies
local_context.text: The Hanoi Statistics Office publishes monthly and periodic data on foreign investment, industrial production and business formation, which help place a counterparty in context. The Management Board of Hanoi's High-Tech and Industrial Zones oversees industrial and technology parks, including Hoa Lac. Their announcements on new projects and capital increases help confirm investment claims made by local partners about projects and capital.

tdsc_approach: TDSC handles Hanoi matters from Nashville and has no office, staff or licence in Vietnam. Engagements begin with a review of what can lawfully be established: National Business Registration Portal data, published enterprise notices, Hanoi Stock Exchange and regulator disclosures, court and arbitration information available through counsel, Vietnamese-language press and international records. Because we have not identified a licensing regime for private investigators in Vietnam and inquiries into officials or state bodies can be sensitive, TDSC does not commission surveillance or approaches to officials. Any local enquiries are scoped with Vietnamese counsel, and personal data is handled with Vietnam's data protection law in mind.

faqs.q: Can we check a Hanoi company's registration details?
faqs.a: Yes, to a point. The National Business Registration Portal shows basic registration data, including the enterprise code, address, legal representative and published notices of changes. Shareholder detail, financial statements and some licences are not always public and are often obtained through counsel or from the company itself, so diligence combines registry data with other sources.

faqs.q: Why does state ownership matter in Hanoi counterparty research?
faqs.a: Many large Hanoi companies are state-owned groups, their subsidiaries or businesses dependent on public contracts and land allocations. Identifying state shareholders, former officials in management and reliance on public approvals helps clients assess anti-corruption risk and understand how stable a partner's position is, particularly given the scale of recent anti-corruption enforcement.

faqs.q: Is VIAC the usual arbitral institution for disputes with Hanoi companies?
faqs.a: VIAC is the best known institution in Vietnam and is frequently chosen, though other centres, including a new Hanoi branch of the Southern Trade Arbitration Center, also operate. Awards can be set aside by Vietnamese courts, including where a dispute is found not to be commercial. Institution and seat are matters for counsel.

faqs.q: Can TDSC verify a factory or supplier near Hanoi?
faqs.a: TDSC can verify a supplier's registration, ownership, related parties, litigation and reputation through documentary and open sources. Where a site visit is needed, it is scoped with the client and Vietnamese counsel and limited to lawful, open activity such as a declared visit, rather than covert observation, which is not appropriate in Vietnam.

faqs.q: Which court would hear a commercial dispute with a Hanoi company?
faqs.a: Depending on value, parties and subject matter, a dispute may go to a regional people's court or the Hanoi People's Court, with the court structure reorganised from 1 July 2025. Many foreign parties instead choose arbitration. Counsel determines the forum; TDSC supports either route with party and asset research.
